- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 2–3 points.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts continuation; align forecast with sentiment direction if sentiment > 0.3.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias if sentiment < 0.1.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/– 0.3+), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before final 30d output.
- If recent 18-day price range is narrow (< 2% volatility), model often overpredicts volatility; reduce forecast spread by 20–30% to match sentiment calmness.
